why_winner: B is the only variant that opens on an indictment the reader has a stake in arguing with, which is exactly the hook property the tracker credits for the account's strongest posts and the property the 2.48% routines post lacked. It also carries two pieces of real build evidence without turning the post into a narration of the author's own system.

runner_up_notes.A: The opening two lines are the strongest concrete image in any variant: a finished-looking app where nothing works. Worth grafting as the proof beat under B's claim, compressed to two lines.
runner_up_notes.C: The five-line diagnostic is the single most saveable asset produced in this round and is the same self-locating shape as the account's top performer. It belongs on a deck slide, with one line teased in the caption to earn the swipe.

issues.description: At 291 words the winner reproduces the full five-rung list and the full ordering rule, which are deck slides 2 and 6. On a document post a caption that already teaches the content removes the reason to swipe, and swipe depth is the only thing this format is being tested for.
issues.action: Cut to roughly 130 to 160 words. Remove the numbered five-rung list and the four-step ordering sequence from the caption entirely, both are carried by the deck. Keep the claim, one compressed proof beat, the load-bearing rule stated once, and the CTA.

issues.description: The load-bearing rule, that a rung only holds if the rung below it is reliable, arrives in line nine after the full list. It is the thesis of the post and the tagline of the deck.
issues.action: Move it up so it lands immediately after the opening claim and its one-line reason, before any evidence.

issues.description: The plan's Performance Context requires a genuinely usable reader-side payoff, since the account's top performer worked by letting readers locate themselves on a path. B currently offers a diagnosis with no self-check the reader can run.
issues.action: Graft one line from C as a swipe hook, naming the rung-1 and rung-5 symptoms only, and point explicitly at the deck for the rest of the diagnostic.

issues.description: The phrase 'Not because they picked the wrong tool. Because they jumped.' is the sharpest line in the draft but sits as a throwaway second beat.
issues.action: Keep it as the second line and let it carry the turn into the rule. No rewrite needed, just protect it during the cut.
